versions.short: The bill would add penalties for certain tax-exempt organizations that make political contributions after receiving money from foreign nationals. Such an organization would owe a tax penalty equal to twice the amount of a contribution it makes to a political committee or to a certain type of tax-exempt social welfare group, if it received a gift or contribution from a foreign national during the two years before that contribution. The rules would apply to organizations that file annual returns and have gross receipts or assets above set thresholds, and an organization could rely on a donor's stated nationality unless it knew or should have known the statement was false. The bill would also set escalating taxes on repeat offenders, with a second offense taxed at a higher rate and any later offense also costing the organization its tax-exempt status for two years. These changes would take effect one year after the bill is enacted.
